summary: Construct the Smith restriction functor from equivariant étale sheaves to a cyclic Tate quotient, its relative localization and six-operation comparisons, and the normalized integral Tate-parity lifting used in cyclic Satake base change. The final comparison identifies this functor with diagonal restriction of tilting representations under modular equal-characteristic geometric Satake. The plan separates valid ordinary coefficient reduction from false equivariant fullness, character equality from natural dual-group equivariance, and objectwise integral comparisons from their unresolved naturality. It also owns the general algebra Tate diagonal and Frobenius linearization needed by the global and local consumers.

nodes.title: Coefficient and cyclic-action conventions
nodes.statement: A coefficient datum consists of an odd prime p, a separably closed geometric field F with p invertible, k=an algebraic closure of F_p, O=W(k), and C_p with specified generator σ. Use Λ=k, O/p^m or O, as individually stated. Write A_Λ=Λ[C_p] and N=Σ_{i=0}^{p−1}σ^i. Ordinary coefficient actions are Λ-linear; arithmetic semilinear actions are separately marked. Goodness means p does not divide any coefficient of a highest root in each irreducible dual root system. Type A has no excluded primes, B/C/D exclude 2, G₂/F₄/E₆/E₇ exclude 2,3, and E₈ excludes 2,3,5.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: The notation section fixes k as an algebraic closure of F_p with the discrete topology, geometry over fields of characteristic different from p with p-adically complete coefficients, σ as a chosen generator of a cyclic group of order p, and N as the sum of its powers. Section 4.6.1 sets up G=H^p with cyclic rotation and, after Lemma 4.11, assumes p odd and good for the dual group. Goodness is used there without being defined; the highest-root definition and its type table recorded in this node are the standard ones.

proofSteps: Use the existing Witt ring and dual-root-datum carriers. Prove the good-prime predicate is invariant under duality of root systems and products. Coefficients are discrete at torsion level; O is an adic coefficient system, not a discrete torsion ring.
acceptance: p=3 is odd and good for GL₂, but not good for G₂.
On a trivial O-module N is multiplication by p; on a regular orbit N is the orbit sum, not zero.
O/p identifies with k, whereas O itself has characteristic zero.

nodes.title: Admissible geometric actions
nodes.statement: For a separated locally finite type F-scheme Y, an admissible C_p-action is an action for which every orbit is contained in an invariant affine open; equivalently use an invariant affine open cover in the cases considered. Define Y^σ as the scheme-theoretic equalizer of σ and identity, and Y/C_p as the glued affine invariant quotient. The complement of Y^σ is a free C_p-space because p is prime; in characteristic different from p its quotient is a finite étale C_p-torsor. For ind-schemes require an invariant closed filtration by finite-type pieces.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Section 3.2 works with a separated locally finite type scheme carrying a σ-action that is admissible in the sense of SGA 1, Exposé V, Definition 1.7, and notes (after Riche–Williamson) that this holds when the scheme is exhausted by quasi-projective pieces. Lemma 3.6 uses admissibility to form the quotient by a free action as a map of schemes. The node adds the fixed-point and free-complement facts these statements use.

proofSteps: Import finite-quotient representability and its universal property; check the prime-order stabilizer dichotomy and étaleness of the free quotient. Specify compatible bounded pieces before using an ind-scheme.

nodes.title: Equivariant and ind-constructible derived categories
nodes.statement: Set D_σ(Y;Λ)=D([Y/C_p];Λ) in the imported enhanced étale sheaf theory. Its bounded constructible subcategory has bounded constructible cohomology on Y; ind-constructible means the filtered-colimit enlargement with a uniform cohomological bound on the bounded part. If the geometric action is trivial, identify this with the derived category of sheaves of A_Λ-modules. For a nontrivial action keep the quotient-stack category: a coefficient C_p-action alone is different. Extra L^+G-equivariance means equivariant derived sheaves before passage to the constructible homotopy category; parentheses around L^+G mean constructibility for its orbits after forgetting this extra equivariance.

nodes.title: Arbitrary flat cyclic group-ring modules
nodes.statement: For any field k of characteristic p, k[C_p]≅k[u]/(u^p) by σ↦1+u. It is a commutative Artinian local ring with maximal ideal (u) and residue field k. Every flat module over it is free, without a finite-generation hypothesis. More generally a flat module over a commutative local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal is free.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma 10.101.2 shows that over a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal the flat, free and projective modules coincide, with no finiteness hypothesis. Lemma 10.101.1 gives the basis-lifting criterion behind it, and Lemma 10.101.3 the version for a nilpotent ideal of an arbitrary ring.

Feng cites this tag to say that a k[σ]-module is flat exactly when it is free, so that Tate cohomology of complexes descends to the Tate category. The proof of Lemma 3.2 uses the same fact for the Artinian ring k[σ].

proofSteps: Choose a basis of M/mM and lift it. Nilpotence proves generation without finite Nakayama; flatness annihilates the kernel after reduction and nilpotence annihilates that kernel. For the group algebra use the binomial identity in characteristic p and compare bases. The pinned finite-flat theorem checks the finitely generated special case but is insufficient for arbitrary stalks.
acceptance: For p=3 the algebra is k[u]/u³; its regular module is flat/free, while the residue module k is not flat. An infinite direct sum of regular modules is also covered; the finite-flat library theorem alone does not prove this case.

nodes.title: Flat and perfect equivariant complexes
nodes.statement: For trivial geometric action on Y, Flat^b(Y;A_Λ) is the full thick subcategory of complexes locally represented by bounded complexes of flat A_Λ-sheaves with finite Tor amplitude locally on Y; the globally bounded variant requires a uniform bound on the chosen bounded-dimensional piece. Perf_c is its intersection with D^b_c. On a point with finite modules, perfect means a bounded complex of finite projectives. For a nontrivial geometric action retain D_σ(Y;Λ); the group-ring flat kernel is imposed only on a trivially acted-on base or on the fixed locus, rather than identifying the source with group-ring sheaves.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Definition 3.1 defines Flat^b as the bounded complexes whose geometric stalks are represented by bounded complexes of flat, not necessarily finite, Λ[σ]-modules. Lemma 3.2 identifies Flat^b, for Λ=k, with the objects of locally finite Tor amplitude. The converse direction rests on showing that a stalkwise finite Tor amplitude is uniformly bounded.

proofSteps: Specify the local versus uniform bounds separately. Use K-flat replacements rather than termwise tensoring an arbitrary representative; form the full stable subcategory.
acceptance: A free regular module and all its shifts lie in the kernel; the trivial k[C_p]-module k does not.
The cone of any morphism between flat bounded complexes remains in the thick kernel.
Finite Tor dimension must be over A_Λ: k is Λ-flat when Λ=k, but is not A_k-flat.

nodes.title: Flat resolutions and stalkwise Tor detection
nodes.statement: For A_Λ-sheaves on an étale topos, Tor amplitude [a,b] is detected on geometric stalks with the same interval and is equivalent to a flat representative with that amplitude in the bounded setting. Over the Artinian rings k[C_p] and (O/p^m)[C_p], a bounded finite-Tor complex has a bounded flat representative. A finite-rank module over these rings of finite projective dimension is projective; the arbitrary-module version uses the nilpotent-local-ring flat criterion, not an appeal to finite generation. Integral O-complexes use finite Tor dimension directly and a separately justified adic passage.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma 21.46.3 says that on a ringed site Tor amplitude in [a,b] is equivalent to a representative by flat modules in degrees [a,b]. Lemma 21.46.10 passes the same interval to stalks, and back when the site has enough points. Definition 15.70.1 defines projective amplitude, and Lemma 10.101.3 is the freeness criterion for a nilpotent ideal.

The proof combines these statements with the vanishing finitistic dimension of k[σ]: a complex in degrees [a,b] whose stalks have finite Tor amplitude has amplitude [a,b] at every stalk, hence globally.

proofSteps: Use the imported K-flat resolution and the exactness/conservativity of geometric stalks to compare derived tensors. Truncate using the Tor-vanishing syzygy criterion. For Artinian rings apply dimension shifting and the nilpotent maximal-ideal criterion to the last syzygy. Do not infer an integral uniform estimate merely from an Artinian finite-level calculation.
acceptance: For the two-term regular complex [A→^{u}A] over A=k[u]/u^p, finite Tor amplitude holds although its nonzero cohomology modules are not flat. Keep a common interval at every stalk; individually finite intervals on a disjoint union do not give a bounded global one.

nodes.title: Constructible and bounded ind Tate categories
nodes.statement: For trivial geometric action and Λ=k or O, define Perf(Y;TΛ)=D^b_c(Y;A_Λ)/Perf_c(Y;A_Λ) and Shv(Y;TΛ)=D^b_ind(Y;A_Λ)/Flat^b(Y;A_Λ) as stable Verdier localizations, then take their homotopy categories. Write T* for the quotient projections. The word Perf in Perf(Y;TΛ) denotes the constructible quotient, not the subcategory being killed. Its map to Shv(Y;TΛ) is conservative under the stalkwise finite-Tor criterion. At O-level the conservative comparison is conditional on the uniform adic finite-Tor criterion G1.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Definition 3.3 defines the constructible Tate category as D^b_c(Y;Λ[σ]) modulo the complexes with perfect stalks, and the bounded ind-constructible one as D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) modulo Flat^b. T* denotes both projections. Display (3.1) is the induced functor from the first to the second, conservative because of Lemma 3.2.

nodes.title: Two-periodicity of the Tate quotient
nodes.statement: For Λ=k or O, there is a natural isomorphism [2]≅Id on these Tate categories, compatible with restriction. It comes from the class Λ→Λ[2] of the periodic C_p-resolution. The cone has a bounded induced A_Λ-resolution; tensoring with a bounded input over Λ remains in Flat^b because Λ has finite global dimension. This is a categorical statement, stronger than the existing isomorphism of Tate groups.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Example 3.4, after Treumann, shows that on the Tate category of a point the shift by two is isomorphic to the identity. It uses the four-term exact sequence built from 1−σ and the norm, whose middle terms are induced. Display (3.5) records the resulting class Λ→Λ[2] in D^b(Λ[σ]). Example 3.4 calls that sequence nullhomotopic, which it is not over the group ring (finding E18).

proofSteps: Construct the periodicity class using N and σ−1 in the existing group cohomology model. Its cone is Λ-perfect and induced over A_Λ. Tensor and check the flat bound, then use the quotient universal property. Normalize the generator so the comparison with the pinned all-degree Tate API has the same norm sign.
acceptance: At a point the trivial k-module survives the quotient and becomes two-periodic; the regular representation becomes zero. The periodicity cone must have induced terms, not a claimed contracting homotopy of the resolution.

nodes.title: Tate cohomology of complexes and sheaves
nodes.statement: For a bounded A_Λ-complex K on a trivially acted-on étale space S, put T^j(K)=colim_n H^{j+2n}(RHom_{A_Λ}(Λ,K)), with transition induced by Λ→Λ[2]. This is an étale sheaf (internal Hom followed by cohomology), not the set of global morphisms. Its coefficient ring is T^0Λ and its index is naturally modulo two. On a point compare this construction with hypercohomology of the existing complete cyclic resolution. For Λ=k or O it annihilates Flat^b and descends to Shv(S;TΛ); the O-adic construction and its uniform comparisons require G1.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Section 3.4.1 defines the Tate cohomology of a bounded-below Λ[σ]-complex as the colimit of Hom(Λ,C[i+2n]) along (3.5). It notes two-periodicity and descent to the derived category, and for Λ=k to the Tate category. Remark 3.13 compares this with Hom in the Tate category. Section 3.4.2 defines Tate cohomology sheaves on a trivially acted-on S by the same colimit of sheaf Hom, as sheaves of T^0Λ-modules.

proofSteps: Use the norm splice already present for modules; extend to bounded complexes by totalization and sheafification. Exact filtered colimits give the sheaf and independence of resolutions. Check vanishing on bounded flat complexes before descending.

nodes.statement: A distinguished triangle K′→K→K″→K′[1] of bounded equivariant complexes produces a functorial long exact sequence of Tate cohomology sheaves, with the connecting map T^jK″→T^{j+1}K′ and period two. After a bounded Rf! the same sequence is the relative Tate sequence.

sources.match: Section 3.4.4 states that a distinguished triangle in D^b_σ(Y;k) gives a periodic long exact sequence of the relative Tate cohomology sheaves T^iRf!.

proofSteps: Apply RHom(Λ,−), take the long exact cohomology sequence and pass to exact filtered colimits. Relative statements additionally require the bounded compact-support theorem of ST.2; this node supplies only the Tate exact-sequence operation.
acceptance: For a short exact sequence of cyclic modules, recover the pinned module Tate connecting map at a point. For a split sequence, its connecting map is zero and the quotient-level statement is additive.

nodes.title: Trivial-action and integral-unit formulas
nodes.statement: For C∈D^b(k) inflated to k[C_p], T^*(C)≅H^*(C)⊗_k T^*(k), with the total grading modulo two. For an O-free module L with trivial action, T^even(L)=L/pL and T^odd(L)=0. On a stratum the latter formula applies to O-free local systems stalkwise, giving the even Tate unit. No claim that every constructible sheaf complex is globally formal is used.

sources.match: Lemma 3.14 says that for a complex inflated from D^b(k) the Tate cohomology is its ordinary cohomology tensored with T^*(k). nodes.title: The stratified integral Tate category
nodes.statement: For a finite stratification S of a finite-type Y, Perf_S(Y;TO) is the essential stable image of D^b_S(Y;O[C_p]) in the constructible Tate quotient; equivalently use its quotient by S-constructible perfect complexes after verifying the restriction functors preserve that kernel. Inflation ε* assigns the trivial coefficient C_p-action to an O-complex. The pariversity is a function S→Z/2, independent of coefficient C_p-actions.

Corollary 4.5.2 proves that the S-constructible derived category of O[σ]-sheaves modulo its S-constructible perfect complexes is equivalent to the S-constructible integral Tate category. The opening of §5 fixes the trivial action and the simply connected strata assumed in the Tate-parity theory.

nodes.title: Separate Tor bounds for compact support and open direct image
nodes.statement: Let A=k[C_p] or (O/p^m)[C_p], and let f:Y→S be separated of finite type, with geometric fibres of dimension ≤d, under the torsion étale projection formula and the bound cd_c(f)≤2d. If K has A-Tor amplitude [a,b], then Rf!K has amplitude [a,b+2d]. For a quasi-compact open immersion j:U→X into a finite-dimensional noetherian scheme, Rj* preserves finite A-Tor dimension when the relevant ambient local étale cohomological dimension is uniformly bounded. Its bound is that ambient bound, not 2 times the relative dimension of j. At adic O-level require one compatible finite-level system, a uniform bound and the derived-limit/projection-formula comparisons.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.9, p.16; proof of Lemma 3.7, pp.15–16
sources.match: Lemma 3.9 asserts that Rf! preserves Flat^b for a separated locally finite type equivariant morphism of bounded dimension. Its proof reduces by filtered colimits to finite type and cites Stacks 0F10 with SGA 4, XVII 5.2.10. The proof of Lemma 3.7 uses that Rj* preserves finite Tor amplitude, citing SGA 4, XVII 5.2.11. The node keeps the corrected separate contracts for the two functors that the PAPER-FENG-24 route brief records from FIX-RT-PAPER-FENG-24.

proofSteps: Tensor with an arbitrary A-module, apply projection formula, then use the compact-support cohomological bound. For j use stalks as cohomology of punctured strict henselian neighborhoods and an ambient bound. The adic comparison is G1, not a formal consequence of these torsion estimates.
acceptance: For A=k[C_p] on A¹, RΓ_c(A¹,A)=A(−1)[−2] attains degree 2. For G_m→A¹, use the Kummer example below to reject a relative-dimension-zero bound on Rj*.

nodes.statement: For a separated equivariant f:Y→S locally of finite type of bounded geometric fibre dimension, construct Rf! from the directed system of quasi-compact opens of Y over finite-type opens of S, using extension by zero and the imported enhanced compact-support functors. A bounded input with a uniform degree interval has a bounded ind-constructible output under a common 2d bound. Constructibility of the output requires the additional usual finite-type and constructible-input hypotheses.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

nodes.title: A free geometric quotient produces flat complexes
nodes.statement: If C_p acts freely and admissibly on Y, q:Y→Y/C_p is its finite étale quotient and E∈D^b_σ(Y;Λ) has finite Λ-Tor dimension, then q_*E, with its quotient C_p-action, has locally a bounded induced A_Λ-resolution and is flat over A_Λ. For Λ=k the coefficient Tor hypothesis is automatic. The hypothesis is geometric equivariance, not a second independent C_p-action on an arbitrary sheaf.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma 3.6 says that for a free σ-action with quotient q the pushforward q_*F is flat over Λ[σ]. The reason is that its stalk is a stalk of F tensored with Λ[σ]. That stalk formula presupposes geometric equivariance (finding E16).

proofSteps: Étale locally trivialize the torsor; descent identifies E with identical coefficient complexes on p sheets. Pushforward is induction from Λ to A_Λ. Tensor a Λ-flat resolution with the regular representation.
acceptance: For p disjoint points permuted cyclically and an equivariant constant Λ-sheaf, q_* gives the regular Λ[C_p]-module. Giving p constant summands an unrelated trivial coefficient action fails this test.

nodes.title: The nearby free complement has flat fixed stalks
nodes.statement: Let i:Y^σ→Y and j:U=Y\Y^σ→Y, with Y separated finite-dimensional of finite type and admissible C_p-action. For E∈D^b_σ(U;Λ) with the stated finite coefficient Tor bounds, the fixed stalks of i*Rj*E have finite A_Λ-Tor dimension with a uniform ambient bound. In the O-adic case this uses G1.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma 3.7 says that, for U the complement of the fixed locus, the stalks of Rj*F at fixed geometric points have finite Tor amplitude over Λ[σ]. The proof uses total ramification of Y→Y/σ at fixed points, the free-quotient lemma, and preservation of finite Tor amplitude by Rj*.

proofSteps: Factor the open complement through its free finite quotient, apply the regular-module calculation there, and compute Rj* on strict local neighborhoods. Apply the ambient local cohomological bound, not a relative-dimension-zero bound.
acceptance: For scalar rotation on A¹ the fixed-origin nearby stalk is [k[C_p]→^{1−σ}k[C_p]], a perfect complex with two nonflat cohomology modules. This tests the complex criterion rather than a false cohomology-wise freeness claim.

nodes.title: Extraordinary and ordinary fixed restriction agree in the quotient
nodes.statement: For a bounded-dimensional Y as in the previous node and E∈D^b_σ(Y;Λ), with the indicated coefficient finite-Tor/adic assumptions, the cone of the natural map i!E→i*E lies in Flat^b(Y^σ;A_Λ). Thus T*i!E≅T*i*E naturally. On finite-type constructible objects the cone is perfect and the comparison is in Perf(Y^σ;TΛ).
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma 3.8 says that the cone of i^!F→i^*F lies in Flat^b(Y^σ;Λ[σ]). The proof restricts the triangle i_*i^!F→F→j_*j^*F to the fixed locus and applies Lemma 3.7. Finding E17 adds the bounded-dimension hypothesis without which the cone need not be bounded.

proofSteps: Restrict the open–closed localization triangle to Y^σ. Its error term is i*Rj*j*E, treated by the previous node. The dimension bound is required for this term to be globally bounded.
acceptance: For trivial action i=id the comparison is identity. For scalar rotation on A¹ its cone is the perfect nearby complex. The disjoint union of A^n tests why a uniform dimension hypothesis is required.

nodes.title: The Smith operation
nodes.statement: For i:Y^σ→Y define Psm(E)=T*i*E from D^b_σ(Y;Λ) to Shv(Y^σ;TΛ), and from the constructible source to Perf(Y^σ;TΛ). The fixed locus has trivial geometric action, so the target group-ring category is available. Under the hypotheses of fixed-restrictions there is also the natural presentation T*i!E.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Displays (3.3) and (3.4) define the Smith operation Psm as T* composed with restriction to the fixed locus, from constructible and ind-constructible equivariant sheaves to the corresponding Tate categories. They use (3.2) to view sheaves on Y^σ as Λ[σ]-sheaves. Remark 3.5 checks that the two versions agree.

proofSteps: Compose ordinary fixed-locus pullback with localization. Keep its alternative !-presentation as a theorem with bounds, not an unconditional part of the definition.

For a free geometric action the fixed locus is empty, hence Psm is zero.
On A¹ with x↦ζx and constant k, Psm has the nonzero trivial Tate unit at 0.

nodes.statement: For f between trivially C_p-acted-on schemes and finite-Tor bounds as in finite-tor-pushforward, Rf! carries Flat^b(Y;A_Λ) to Flat^b(S;A_Λ). For a free admissible geometric action on Y and a C_p-equivariant map f:Y→S with trivial action on S, Rf!E is flat over A_Λ for any bounded equivariant E with the needed coefficient bounds. For nontrivial S the statement is instead applied to the base change over S^σ.

sources.match: Lemma 3.9 says compact-support pushforward preserves Flat^b. Corollary 3.11 says that if σ acts trivially on S and freely on Y, then Rf! of any equivariant complex is flat, by factoring through the free quotient. Its printed target should be on S, not Y (finding E15).

proofSteps: The first assertion is the projection formula/Tor bound. For a free source factor through q and apply the first assertion to q*E. The base of a flat quotient assertion is S^σ, not Y.

nodes.title: Operations on Tate categories
nodes.statement: Between trivially acted-on finite-dimensional spaces, descend pullback, bounded compact-support pushforward, tensor and the compatible constructible duality to the designated Tate quotients. With finite-Tor constructible coefficients, define f! and Rf* by the dual formulas and identify them with the descent of the ordinary operations where that descent is established. Internal Hom descends in a variable when the other is Λ-perfect. These are functors on their specified bounded domains; arbitrary unbounded Rf* is not asserted.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Sections 3.3.1–3.3.2 descend pullback and compact-support pushforward to the Tate categories. Appendix A.1 recalls, from Treumann and Riche–Williamson, that pullback, proper pushforward and Verdier duality descend to the constructible Tate categories. It defines f^! and Rf_* by conjugating with duality, and lists the compatibilities of Psm with all four operations in A.1.1–A.1.2.

proofSteps: Check that each operation annihilates the quotient kernel before descending. For duality use finite coefficient Tor dimension and the imported biduality theorem. Derive !-pullback and *-pushforward compatibilities by duality; keep all boundedness hypotheses in the functor signatures.
acceptance: Pullback along an identity and the descended identity agree as functors.
Projection formula with the Tate unit recovers the original object, whereas tensor with a regular A_Λ-module becomes zero.
For a proper f the ! and * pushforwards agree; for a nonproper f they retain their distinct compact-support meanings.

nodes.title: Smith commutes with compact supports
nodes.statement: Let f:Y→S be a separated admissibly C_p-equivariant locally finite type morphism between bounded-dimensional schemes, with the uniform cohomological and coefficient Tor hypotheses above. There is a natural equivalence Psm_S Rf!≅R(f^σ)! Psm_Y. For finite-type constructible inputs this is in the constructible Tate category. Proper pushforward is a special case; properness is not needed for the !-version.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Proposition 3.12 says Psm commutes with compact-support pushforward along an equivariant locally finite type morphism of bounded dimension. Its proof replaces S by S^σ and kills the free complement using Corollary 3.11. Section 3.4.5 restates the result as Psm(Rf!F)≅R(f|_{Y^σ})!Psm(F).

proofSteps: Base change first to S^σ. In that fibre, remove Y^σ using open–closed localization. The complement has a free C_p-action; its compact-support image is flat and vanishes in the quotient. The resulting natural transformation is invertible; verify coherence with composition.
acceptance: For the structure map of the free p-point orbit both sides are zero. For the identity map the comparison is the identity natural transformation, including on a nonzero scalar morphism.

nodes.title: Equivariant localization of cohomology
nodes.statement: For S=Spec(F) with trivial action, the previous equivalence gives T*RΓ_c(Y,E)≅RΓ_c(Y^σ,Psm(E)) in Shv(pt;TΛ). Applying T^j gives the two-periodic localization on cohomology. This is a quotient-level natural isomorphism before extracting groups, and requires all the boundedness hypotheses of smith-pushforward.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Display (3.6) specializes Proposition 3.12 to the structure map to a separably closed point with trivial action, giving T*RΓ_c(Y;F)≅RΓ_c(Y^σ;Psm F). Feng presents this as the sheaf form of the classical localization theorems of Smith theory.

proofSteps: Specialize f to the structure map and use the trivial-action identification of Smith at a point. Pass to relative Tate cohomology; do not identify it with an ordinary non-equivariant cohomology group without the trivial-action formula.
acceptance: For Y the disjoint union of one fixed point and one free orbit, equivariant constant k-coefficients localize to precisely the fixed point. Compare both parity indices with module Tate cohomology.

nodes.title: Modular equal-characteristic geometric Satake
nodes.statement: For a connected reductive H over separably closed F of characteristic different from p, the spherical perverse category P_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k) with fusion commutativity is tensor-equivalent to finite-dimensional rational Rep_k(Ĥ), where Ĥ is the pinned integral dual group base changed to k. The O-flat perverse subcategory has the corresponding tensor equivalence with finite free O-representations of Ĥ_O. The geometry is the scheme-theoretic equal-characteristic affine Grassmannian, not the B_dR^+ Grassmannian. The fibre functor is total cohomology with the usual parity sign correction to symmetry.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Proposition 11.1, p.31; Theorem 12.1, p.33; Theorem 14.1, p.40
sources.match: For a Noetherian coefficient ring of finite global dimension, Proposition 11.1 builds a flat affine group scheme whose representations, finitely generated over the coefficients, form the spherical perverse category, compatibly with base change from Z. Theorem 12.1 identifies the Z-form with the split reductive group of dual root datum. Theorem 14.1 gives the étale variant for coefficients obtained by base change from Z_ℓ.

sources.locator: opening of §4, p.19; §4.5, p.23; Remark A.1, p.58
sources.match: Feng uses the Geometric Satake equivalence with k-coefficients for the scheme-theoretic Grassmannian over F throughout §4. Remark A.1 says this modular equal-characteristic setting is not completely documented and that the complex and B_dR^+ proofs carry over; the node makes that transport an explicit obligation (G2).

proofSteps: Reuse the existing BD Grassmannian, bounded Schubert geometry and fusion correspondences. Prove weight-functor exactness and tensor compatibility with torsion/integral coefficients by the semi-infinite dimension estimates and Künneth formula. Reconstruct the integral Hopf algebra using projective generators on finite Schubert unions, prove base change, and identify its root datum with the already owned dual group. MV07 Theorem 14.1 gives the étale variant; explicitly supply the O-adic extension using compatible finite levels, and separably closed to algebraically closed invariance. G2 records these coefficient/transport obligations.
acceptance: For a split torus, point sheaves indexed by coweights correspond to one-dimensional characters; fusion adds coweights. For H=PGL₂ the IC/parity representation of the dual SL₂ has the expected highest weight, so using the original root datum instead of the dual is detected.

nodes.title: Satake standards and coefficient change
nodes.statement: Fix a Borel and dominant λ. Under modular-satake, the perverse standard ^pj_!Λ[dim Gr^λ] corresponds to the Weyl module Δ(λ), and the perverse costandard ^pj_*Λ[dim Gr^λ] to ∇(λ), with the canonical highest-weight map matched. On O-flat objects the k-reduction comparison is derived tensor k⊗^L_O, with ordinary representation reduction on the other side. Do not assert that derived reduction of an arbitrary integral perverse object stays in the perverse heart.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Proposition 13.1 says that under the integral Satake equivalence the map from the standard to the costandard sheaf of λ corresponds to the map from the Weyl module to the induced module. Both are characterized by universal properties in the subcategory with weights at most λ. Corollary 13.2 identifies the ν-weight spaces of both modules with the span of the irreducible components of Gr^λ∩S_ν.
Feng recalls tilting modules as the objects of Rep_k(Ĝ) with both a standard and a costandard filtration, which on the sheaf side requires this standard/costandard comparison.

proofSteps: Use the universal properties on each saturated highest-weight ideal, evaluated by the λ-weight functor. Compare standard/costandard maps and integral projective generators before extending scalars. Track derived tensor for torsion objects.
acceptance: At λ=0 both standard and costandard are the unit. For dual SL₂ in characteristic 3, distinguish Δ(3) from ∇(3); do not identify them by semisimplicity or an integral arbitrary-object reduction argument.

nodes.title: The category of rational tilting representations
nodes.statement: Using the Weyl and dual-Weyl modules and highest-weight filtrations requested from the integral highest-weight extension of Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 9, Tilt_Λ(Ĥ) is the full additive subcategory of finite free rational Ĥ_Λ-modules admitting both a finite Δ-filtration and a finite ∇-filtration. For Λ=k, finite free means finite-dimensional. Its exact structure is inherited from rational representations; it is closed under direct summands, not under all kernels and cokernels. Use the integral reductive group representation carrier, not arbitrary representations of the discrete group of k-points.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Section 1.1 recalls tilting modules for a reductive group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p as modules with Weyl and good filtrations. Theorem 1.1 classifies the indecomposable ones as T(λ) by highest weight.
Feng defines Tilt_k(Ĝ) as the full subcategory of Rep_k(Ĝ) of modules with both a standard and a costandard filtration, closed under direct sums and, by a nontrivial theorem, tensor products.

proofSteps: Import the highest-weight predicates, and define their intersection as a full subcategory. API must preserve the algebraic comodule structure on every morphism.
acceptance: The trivial representation is tilting, with both filtrations of length one.
For a split torus every finite-dimensional rational representation is tilting, with its finite character decomposition.

For SL₂ in characteristic 3, the Weyl module Δ(3) has an exact sequence 0→L(1)→Δ(3)→L(3)→0 of two-dimensional simple factors; ∇(3) has the reversed Loewy layers. Thus Δ(3) is not tilting, while T(3) has character ch Δ(3)+ch Δ(1) and dimension 6.

nodes.title: Tensor closure and character determination
nodes.statement: Tensor products of finite-dimensional rational tilting modules for a split connected reductive group over k are tilting. For a product group, external tensor products of indecomposable tiltings give its indecomposable tiltings. The characters ch T(λ) are triangular with leading dominant weight λ of multiplicity one, so equal characters imply isomorphism for finite direct sums of tiltings. Restriction to a maximal torus is faithful, but it is generally not full.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Theorem 1.2 states that tensor products of tilting modules are tilting. In the appendix, Theorem 5.3 shows this is equivalent to Theorem 5.1, the theorem of Donkin, Wang and Mathieu that tensor products of modules with good filtrations have good filtrations.

Footnote 11 uses the tensor theorem to see that diagonal restriction preserves tilting. Section A.4 cites Donkin for faithfulness of restriction to the dual torus and for tilting modules being determined by their characters.

proofSteps: Request the precise good-filtration tensor theorem (Donkin, Wang, Mathieu) and its dual from the integral highest-weight extension of ReductiveGroups Layer 9; no parameter-stack hypothesis is imposed on this generic representation theorem. Krull–Schmidt and the triangular highest-weight characters determine multiplicities recursively. Restriction forgets structure and is faithful; no inference of fullness is allowed.
acceptance: For dual SL₂ in characteristic 3, the standard two-dimensional tilting module has tensor square T(2)⊕T(0). Torus restriction is faithful but its diagonal weight-space endomorphisms need not be SL₂-intertwiners.

nodes.title: Tiltings generate bounded rational derived categories
nodes.statement: The canonical functor K^b(Tilt_k(Ĥ))→D^b(Rep_k(Ĥ)) is an equivalence, where Rep denotes finite-dimensional rational representations. Prove this first inside each finite saturated highest-weight ideal and then pass to their filtered union; this does not give a uniform tilting-resolution length for all highest weights.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Proposition 4.10, citing Riche, states that the bounded homotopy category of tilting modules maps by an equivalence onto D^b(Rep_k(Ĝ)), as for any highest-weight category.

proofSteps: Within a finite highest-weight ideal, Ext^n(T,T′)=0 for n>0 by Δ/∇ Ext-vanishing, giving full faithfulness of the homotopy functor. Resolve standards by tiltings inductively on the finite weight poset; standards generate its bounded derived category. Any bounded complex involves finitely many weights and fits in such an ideal. Request the finite-ideal highest-weight theorem from the integral highest-weight extension of ReductiveGroups Layer 9.
acceptance: For a torus the category is semisimple and degree-zero objects already generate by characters. For a nonsemisimple finite highest-weight ideal, check full faithfulness through Ext^{>0}(tilting,tilting)=0 and generation via finite standard/costandard resolutions.

nodes.title: Even stratifications and pariversities
nodes.statement: A JMW stratification S of Y has finitely many connected smooth locally closed strata, the usual frontier condition, and the following coefficient condition for Λ=k or O: for finite free local systems L,L′ on each stratum, every Ext^n(L,L′) is finite free over Λ and vanishes for odd n. A pariversity † assigns an element of Z/2 to each stratum; the dimension pariversity is dim(Y_λ) mod 2. Simple connectivity is an additional hypothesis used for lifting, not part of the general definition. The class of local systems is part of the data: over a base field of positive characteristic it is taken to be the constant (or group-equivariant) ones, since wild local systems on affine strata can have odd cohomology.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Section 2.1 fixes a field or complete discrete valuation ring as coefficients and a stratified variety. It assumes (2.1)–(2.2): Hom between free local systems on a stratum vanishes in odd degrees and is free in all degrees. Definition 2.3, at the start of §2.2, introduces pariversities.

Section 4.1 calls a stratification JMW under the same odd-vanishing and freeness condition, notes that it holds for affine flag varieties (JMW14 §4.1), and fixes the dimension pariversity. Over a base field of positive characteristic the claim for affine flag varieties holds only for constant local systems (finding E38). The sentence after (4.1), in §4.2 on p.20, misstates the parity condition (finding E23).

proofSteps: Use local-system Ext in the imported constructible derived category. Require freeness and odd vanishing; even nonzero Ext is allowed. Keep all local systems if strata are not simply connected.
acceptance: An affine space with constant coefficients satisfies the condition; its dimension changes † but not the odd-Ext vanishing.
P¹ with its one smooth stratum has nonzero H², which is allowed; a smooth elliptic curve with H¹≠0 fails the condition for the constant local system.
The same stratification can be used with constant †=0 and dimension †; on a one-dimensional stratum these give different even objects.

nodes.title: Parity complexes and parity sheaves
nodes.statement: An object E∈D^b_S(Y;Λ) is *-even for † if each i_λ*E has finite free local-system cohomology only in degrees congruent to †(λ); !-even uses i_λ!E. Even means both, odd means E[1] is even, and parity means a direct sum of an even and an odd object. A parity sheaf E(λ,L) is an indecomposable parity object supported on closure(Y_λ) whose restriction to Y_λ is L[dim Y_λ], for an indecomposable finite free local system L. Existence is an independent theorem.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

nodes.title: Uniqueness and Krull–Schmidt for parity extensions
nodes.statement: In the finite JMW setting with complete local coefficient ring Λ, parity objects have Krull–Schmidt decompositions. Every indecomposable parity object has one irreducible support closure(Y_λ), restricts there to one indecomposable local system shifted by an integer, and is determined up to isomorphism by that restriction and support. This proves uniqueness of E(λ,L), not its existence.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Remark 2.1 notes that the constructible derived category is Krull–Remak–Schmidt for the complete local coefficient rings considered. Theorem 2.12 gives irreducible support and uniqueness of an indecomposable parity complex with a given dense-stratum restriction.
Theorem 4.1 restates JMW14 Theorem 2.12 and observes that uniqueness does not give existence.

proofSteps: Induct over strata using odd-Hom vanishing to extend maps between restrictions. Endomorphism rings of finite-support parity objects are finite over the complete local coefficient ring, so idempotents split and the usual local-ring criterion gives Krull–Schmidt. The dense-stratum inverse lifts modulo the boundary radical.
acceptance: On a point over complete local O, the only normalized rank-one extension is O. Uniqueness must not imply existence for an arbitrary stratified singular variety; the Grassmannian existence theorem is an additional input.

nodes.title: Parity extensions on the equal-characteristic Grassmannian
nodes.statement: The L^+H-orbit stratification of every finite Schubert union in Gr_H satisfies the JMW condition for Λ=k,O with constant local systems on the strata, equivalently L^+H-equivariant ones, since the stabilizers are connected; these are the only local systems used. In characteristic 0 the strata are simply connected. Over a field of positive characteristic ℓ the condition fails for arbitrary étale local systems (finding E38), so the orbit-constructible category is taken with constant restrictions to strata. Its normalized parity extensions exist for all dominant coweights and trivial finite free local systems. They admit compatible L^+H-equivariant structures in the precise non-torsion-prime setting of JMW16 Theorem 1.4. Under the odd good-prime hypothesis of Feng24, prove that the orbit-constructible normalized category used below has the required equivariant realization; do not identify the full equivariant derived category with the orbit-constructible one.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Feng states that parity sheaves exist on Gr_G for the positive-loop orbit stratification and can be made equivariant when p is not a torsion prime, citing JMW16 Theorem 1.4. Section 4.5 notes that the orbit stratification of this Kac–Moody flag variety is JMW, which in positive characteristic needs the constant-local-system convention (finding E38).

Theorem 1.4, from JMW14 Theorem 4.6, gives for characteristic not a torsion prime a unique indecomposable equivariant parity complex with support the closure of Gr^λ and constant rank-one restriction there. Every indecomposable parity complex is of this form. Footnote 3 says the torsion restriction can be removed in the non-equivariant setting.

proofSteps: Build Bott–Samelson parity pushforwards on affine flag varieties, then take the appropriate summands on the partial flag/Grassmannian. Check evenness, the local-system condition and integral lifting on each bounded piece. Compare étale and complex proofs, including non-torsion/good-prime equivariance and passage to separably closed F. These proof inputs are the explicit transport contract G2.
acceptance: For a torus every stratum is a point and its extension is Λ. For a GL₂ minuscule closed Schubert P¹ the normalized extension is Λ[1]. Check ordinary Hom separately from equivariant Hom.

Over an algebraic closure of F_ℓ, a one-dimensional Schubert cell of the affine flag variety is A¹, and the Artin–Schreier sheaf L_ψ(x^d), for d≥3 prime to ℓ and ψ a nontrivial character of F_ℓ into k^×, has H¹ of dimension d−1. The constant-local-system convention excludes it.

nodes.title: Normalized parity sheaves are tilting Satake objects
nodes.statement: For odd p good for the root system of Ĥ (equivalently H), every normalized k- or O-parity sheaf on Gr_H is perverse. Modular Satake induces Parity^0_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;k)≅Tilt_k(Ĥ), with the chosen equivariant realization when required. The integral version uses O-flat perverse sheaves. The characteristic assumption is goodness, not the larger bounds in JMW16 Theorem 1.8.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Theorem 4.8 states that for p good the Satake equivalence restricts to an equivalence between normalized parity sheaves and tilting modules. Its proof sketch transports Mautner–Riche to the Grassmannian over F, replacing one loop-group step by Zhu Lemma 5.2.4. Remark 4.9 mentions the JMW16 Theorem 1.8 route, with worse bounds on p.

Corollary 1.6 states that for p good for the group of the Grassmannian every spherical parity sheaf is perverse. Section 6.5 deduces it from the parity/exotic-tilting equivalence of Theorem 1.1 and a perversity criterion for self-dual objects (Lemma 6.6), after standard reductions to products of simply connected quasi-simple groups not of type A and general linear groups, which satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1.

proofSteps: Use MR18 Theorem 1.1: the mixed/parity affine-Grassmannian category is related to the exotic coherent category on the Springer resolution of the dual group, compatibly with grading and tilting generators. Its Corollary 1.6 establishes perversity for every good prime, reducing along central isogenies and products. The exotic/Soergel proof engine and its étale transport are not supplied by the characteristic-zero Springer roadmap; G3 records this exact missing foundation. Once perversity holds, Δ/∇-filtrations characterize the Satake images as tilting.
acceptance: For the GL₂ minuscule P¹ stratum, k[1] is perverse and maps to the corresponding fundamental tilting representation. Check the hypothesis is odd good p, rather than the larger source-specific sufficient bounds.

nodes.title: External products of normalized Grassmannian parity sheaves
nodes.statement: For G=H^r, every normalized O-parity object on Gr_G≅(Gr_H)^r is a finite direct sum of E(λ₁)⊠⋯⊠E(λ_r). The external product is the normalized indecomposable extension on the product stratum. Its stalk and costalk cohomology are the graded tensor products of the corresponding finite free O-modules, including the Koszul symmetry signs.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: proof of Lemma 4.14, p.24; Theorem 4.8, p.23
sources.match: The proof of Lemma 4.14 reduces an integral Satake object on Gr_G≅(Gr_H)^p, by a filtration, to external products F_1⊠⋯⊠F_p. For the normalized parity inputs used later, this node replaces the filtration (finding E26) by a direct-sum decomposition into external products of parity sheaves, using Theorem 4.8 on each factor.

proofSteps: Use the Künneth theorem for finite free stalks and costalks, and dense-stratum normalization. Indecomposability follows either from the product tilting classification under Satake or from the local endomorphism criterion. This direct-sum decomposition replaces the invalid t-exact filtration argument in the printed proof.
acceptance: The product of the GL₂ minuscule generators is O_{(P¹)^r}[r] and has rank-one dense-stratum restriction. A direct sum of two generators stays a direct sum and is not mislabeled indecomposable.

nodes.title: The graded Hom formula and its composition law
nodes.statement: For bounded constructible O-complexes E,F in the LL integral Tate setting, with trivial coefficient C_p-action and the finite-support coefficient hypotheses, Hom_{Perf(Y;TO)}(T*ε*E,T*ε*F)≅⊕_{i∈Z}Hom_{D^b(Y;k)}(k⊗^L E,(k⊗^L F)[2i]). Composition adds the indices using shifts. Require the stratified version with finite Hom groups and nilpotence of the positive-degree endomorphism ideal for normalized parity inputs. The category is Krull–Schmidt under the finite-stratification, complete-local and simply-connected-strata assumptions used by LL.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Proposition 4.6.1 computes Hom in the integral Tate category between images of O-complexes as the direct sum over i of Hom between their mod-p reductions shifted by 2i. Proposition 5.5.2 shows that the Tate-even categories, and hence the Tate-parity complexes, are Krull–Remak–Schmidt.
Display (4.2) quotes this Hom formula. Feng uses it in the proof of Proposition 4.5 and to define the lifting functor on morphisms.

proofSteps: Compare the periodic complete resolution with derived reduction, then compute quotient morphisms by stabilized Hom. Check naturality and the index-addition composition formula before projecting any grading. Carry the proof through the étale coefficient setting via G2. Finite support and bounded Hom ensure the nonnegative endomorphism algebra has nilpotent positive ideal in the perverse case.
acceptance: For E=O_{P¹}[1], the Tate endomorphisms have index-zero k and index-one H²(P¹;k). Composition of homogeneous classes adds indices; at a point only index zero remains for degree-zero inputs.

nodes.title: Tate parity and Tate-parity sheaves
nodes.statement: In Perf_S(Y;TO), an object K is *-Tate-even when T^{†(λ)+1}(i_λ*K)=0 for each λ, and !-Tate-even uses i_λ!K. Tate-even requires both; Tate-odd means a shift by one is even, and Tate-parity means their direct sum. A Tate-parity sheaf is an indecomposable such object whose dense-stratum restriction is T*ε*L[dim Y_λ] for an indecomposable O-free local system L. The integral coefficient ring O is essential: the mod-p Tate unit has nonzero odd cohomology.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Definition 4.2 defines ∗- and !-Tate-even objects by vanishing of T^{†(λ)+1} of the stratum restrictions, Tate-odd objects by a shift, and Tate-parity complexes as sums of the two. Definition 4.4 defines a Tate-parity sheaf as an indecomposable Tate-parity complex whose dense-stratum restriction is T*ε*L[dim Y_λ].
Definition 5.3.1 is the original definition, phrased as vanishing of T^1 of the restrictions shifted by the pariversity.

nodes.statement: In the finite JMW integral Tate setting with simply connected strata and the stated finite-Hom hypotheses, an indecomposable Tate-parity object has support the closure of one stratum and is determined by its restriction to the dense stratum. Existence is separate. If E(λ,L) is an O-parity sheaf with no negative self-Ext, then T*ε*E is the corresponding indecomposable Tate-parity sheaf.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

Proposition 4.5 (LL21 5.6.3–5.6.4) shows that T*ε* sends even and odd complexes to Tate-even and Tate-odd ones, and a parity sheaf without negative self-Ext to the Tate-parity sheaf. proofSteps: Repeat support induction with Tate odd-Hom vanishing. For the inflated parity sheaf use the graded Hom formula: its degree-zero endomorphism ring is local, negative degrees vanish and the positive ideal is nilpotent. Thus its full endomorphism ring is local.

nodes.title: Modular reduction on the non-equivariant parity category
nodes.statement: For a finite JMW stratification with simply connected strata (in positive characteristic: with the class of constant local systems, for which the same lifting argument applies), suppose all normalized O- and k-parity extensions exist. Then F=k⊗^L_O sends O-parity extensions to the corresponding k-parity extensions; for parity E,F′, Hom_O(E,F′) is finite free and k⊗_O Hom_O(E,F′)≅Hom_k(FE,FF′). Consequently Parity^0_S(Y;O)⊗_O k→Parity^0_S(Y;k) is an equivalence of additive categories. This statement is about the non-C_p-equivariant orbit-constructible category. Arbitrary C_p-equivariant reduction is not full.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Remark 2.7, p.7; display (2.13) and Proposition 2.39, p.17
sources.match: Remark 2.7 records that Hom between parity complexes is free. Display (2.13) shows that for a ∗-parity F and a !-parity G the reduction map from F⊗Hom(F,G) to Hom of the reductions is an isomorphism. Proposition 2.39 shows that reduction sends parity sheaves to parity sheaves.

Lemma 4.16 asserts the reduction equivalence for σ-equivariant normalized parity categories with simply connected strata, citing these facts. The node keeps only the non-equivariant version, which is all that §4.6.3 uses; the equivariant statement fails (finding E25).

proofSteps: Use free even local-system Hom and induction across strata for Hom base change. Complete-local idempotent lifting and the existence/uniqueness of all parity extensions give essential surjectivity. For the equivariant non-example, the O[C_p]-augmentation ideal I has I^{C_p}=0, but (I/pI)^{C_p}≠0. This obstruction cannot be removed by forgetting the difference between equivariant and ordinary Hom.
acceptance: At a point ordinary Hom(O,O) reduces to Hom(k,k). The augmentation ideal I has I^{C_p}=0 but (I/pI)^{C_p}≠0; this rejects full equivariant reduction without affecting the ordinary equivalence.

nodes.title: Normalized parity categories
nodes.statement: Parity^0_S(Y;Λ) is the full additive closure of unshifted normalized parity sheaves E(λ,L). Parity^0_S(Y;TO) is defined similarly using Tate-parity sheaves. For the lifting functor require all parity extensions to exist and the cross-negative-Hom condition Hom(E(λ,L),E(μ,L′)[n])=0 for all pairs and every n<0, together with the same condition after reduction. On Gr_H it follows from perversity, once parity-tilting has been proved.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Definition 4.7 and the paragraph after it, p.22
sources.match: Definition 4.7 defines normalized (Tate-)parity complexes as unshifted sums of (Tate-)parity sheaves. The following paragraph invokes the lifting functor under existence and vanishing negative self-Ext only, which is weaker than the cited theorem needs (finding E37).

Theorem 5.6.6 constructs the lifting functor assuming that all parity sheaves exist and that Hom(E(λ),E(λ′)[n]) vanishes for all pairs λ,λ′ and all n<0. This is the cross-negative-Hom condition the node requires.

proofSteps: Take additive closures without adjoining arbitrary shifts. Distinguish negative self-Ext, enough for individual indecomposability, from cross-negative-Hom, needed for a functor on the whole additive category.
acceptance: On a point Λ in degree zero is normalized; Λ[1] is not.
T*O[2]≅T*O is normalized in the Tate category, but O[2] is not normalized in the ordinary category.
Two perverse parity sheaves have no negative cross-Hom, so the full normalized Grassmannian category satisfies the lifting hypothesis.

nodes.title: The cyclic fixed Grassmannian is diagonal
nodes.statement: For G=H^p with σ rotating factors, Gr_G≅(Gr_H)^p and Gr_G^σ≅Gr_H by the diagonal map, as ind-schemes on test rings. The stratum indexed by (λ₁,…,λ_p) meets this fixed locus exactly when all λ_i are equal, in which case the intersection is Gr_H^λ. Its dimension is d_λ on H and p d_λ on G, so the two dimension pariversities agree for odd p.

sources.match: Lemma 4.11 identifies Gr_H with the σ-fixed subfunctor of Gr_G≅(Gr_H)^p through the diagonal. Section 4.6.3 shows that a Schubert cell of Gr_G meets Gr_H only for a constant tuple, where the intersection is the corresponding Schubert cell of H. For odd p the two dimension pariversities agree, by dim Gr^λ=⟨2ρ,λ⟩.

proofSteps: Apply the product description of loop groups and positive loops to the fppf quotient; test-ring fixed points force all components equal. Use the imported dimension formula d_λ=⟨2ρ,λ⟩. Equality mod two is not equality of the integer shifts.

nodes.title: The cyclic convolution norm
nodes.statement: On the spherical symmetric monoidal category for G=H^p, define Nm(E)=E*σE*⋯*σ^{p−1}E with σ-linearization given by cyclic rotation through the fusion symmetry. On maps take the corresponding product of the σ-translates of a map. Define it on all k-Satake objects and on O-flat normalized parity objects. It is a plain functor to the σ-equivariant category; it is neither additive nor O-linear before Smith projection.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Definition 4.12 defines Nm(F) as the p-fold convolution of the σ-translates of F. Its σ-equivariant structure (4.4) comes from the commutativity constraint, and Feng constructs it in the perverse category before realizing it in the equivariant derived category.
Theorem 1.5, from JMW14 Theorem 4.8, says convolution of parity complexes on the affine Grassmannian is parity. Section 4.6.3 uses this to see that Nm(F) is parity.

proofSteps: Use fusion associativity and the sign-corrected symmetry to construct the cyclic linearization and prove its p-th power is the identity. On normalized parity objects tensor closure under Satake gives closure of the convolution norm.

Nm(a·id_E)=a^p·id_{Nm(E)}, so ordinary scalar linearity fails for general a∈k.
Nm(E⊕F) contains the pure E and pure F terms and mixed cyclic orbits; before quotienting those mixed terms must remain.

nodes.title: Trivial and free cyclic summands in norm stalks
nodes.statement: For E a normalized O-parity object on Gr_{H^p}, the stalk and costalk cohomology of Nm(E) at every diagonal fixed point has a C_p-stable filtration whose associated graded is a direct sum of trivial O-free modules and free O[C_p]-modules. The statement here is restricted to the normalized Grassmannian parity objects used in BC. It does not assert the printed Lemma 4.14 for every integral Satake object.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma 4.14 states that, for F with free stalk and costalk cohomology, the fixed-point stalk and costalk cohomology of Nm(F) have σ-stable filtrations with trivial or free graded pieces. The decisive step is the external-product case: the stalk is a tensor induction, and a tensor basis splits into fixed and free σ-orbits. The node keeps that step and drops the filtration reduction (finding E26).

proofSteps: Decompose E into finite sums of external products of normalized parity extensions. For one external product, rotation and factorwise convolution give an external p-th power of a single parity object on H, whose finite free stalk and costalk cohomology have a Künneth basis. Cyclic permutation of basis tensors has orbits of size one or p. Koszul signs on a constant p-tuple multiply to +1 for odd p; on a length-p orbit absorb signs into a regular-module basis. Mixed summands from expanding a direct sum form induced cyclic orbits. No perverse filtration is pulled back through i*, and Nm is never applied to an exact sequence as an additive functor.
acceptance: For a stalk with O-basis e₀,e₁ and p=3, the eight tensor words form two fixed words and two free orbits. On an odd-degree basis vector the sign of the length-three cycle is +1. Mixed direct-sum summands are induced.

nodes.title: Smith preserves parity with the cyclic stalk criterion
nodes.statement: Let Y be a finite-dimensional smooth-stratified JMW variety with tame admissible C_p-action preserving each relevant stratum. If E is an equivariant O-parity object and its fixed-point stalk and costalk cohomology have C_p-stable filtrations with trivial O-free or free O[C_p] graded pieces, then Psm(E) is Tate-parity for the induced strata and induced pariversity. Assume the induced fixed stratification is JMW for the classification/lifting applications. Applied to Nm on Gr_{H^p}, this produces normalized Tate parity on Gr_H.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Proposition 4.15, a variant of LL21 Theorem 6.1.1, says that Psm of a parity complex with smooth strata, whose fixed-point stalks and costalks have trivial-or-free filtrations, is Tate-parity for the induced stratification and pariversity. Its proof uses (4.1), the long exact sequence, Lemma 3.8 and the Gysin isomorphism for the smooth fixed strata. Section 4.6.3 applies it to Nm(F) on Gr_G.

proofSteps: For stalks use the trivial/free Tate formulas and the long exact sequence. For costalks use the !-presentation of Smith and the smooth-pair Gysin comparison. A tame finite-order automorphism has smooth fixed subschemes on a smooth stratum: formal lifting obstructions are averaged because p is invertible in F; its tangent is the fixed tangent subspace. The codimension purity shift is even. On the Grassmannian, p d_λ≡d_λ mod 2, while the difference of the two normalization shifts is even and hence disappears only in the Tate quotient.
acceptance: For the norm of a rank-one point sheaf, the fixed stalk is the trivial O-module and becomes the even Tate unit. A free orbit summand becomes zero. Compare the shifted dimension normalization for odd p explicitly.

nodes.title: Additivity and Frobenius semilinearity on morphisms
nodes.statement: On the ordinary normalized O-parity category of Gr_G, D=Psm∘Nm takes values in normalized Tate parity and is additive on objects and morphisms: D(f+g)=D(f)+D(g) and D(a f)=ā^p D(f), for a∈O and ā its image in k. Its canonical biproduct identifications are natural in both arguments. In particular D kills p times every Hom group. Only ordinary source parity morphisms are asserted here, with their norm-generated equivariant morphisms in the intermediate category.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Section 4.6.3 factors L∘Psm∘Nm through the reduction equivalence before additivity on morphisms is available. Section A.3 proves additivity of BC on objects by expanding Nm of a sum into the pure terms plus free σ-orbits, which vanish in the Tate category. The morphism-level additivity and semilinearity stated here is the missing step of finding E27, from the PAPER-FENG-24 review.

proofSteps: Expand the p-fold tensor/convolution product for a biproduct and for (f+g) in the symmetric monoidal category. The two constant words give the pure terms. Since p is prime every other word has an orbit of length p. The mixed sum of morphisms factors through an induced C_p-object; on the fixed locus it is a transfer through a perfect/flat group-ring complex, hence zero after T*. Verify this factorization on maps and its compatibility with composition, not only a direct-sum decomposition of objects. The scalar identity is the product of p copies of a; the integral Tate Hom formula reduces its action to ā^p. The factorization/coherence is a new proof target with these explicit steps, not a claim that Feng proves it.
acceptance: For p=3 check (f+g)^{⊗3}: the six mixed words form two transfers through induced objects. On a scalar a∈O the output scalar is ā³, and a=p gives zero. Perform this calculation on maps, not only objects.

nodes.title: Frobenius twists and linearization of categories
nodes.statement: For a k-linear category C define C^(p) with the same objects and Hom_C(X,Y)⊗_{k,Frob}k, composition induced by tensor product. The tautological functor Fr_C is Frobenius-semilinear and has the universal property for such functors into k-linear categories. If a specific F_p-form C₀ and scalar-extension equivalence are given, define Fr_{C₀}:C→C by fixing C₀ and applying Frobenius to scalars. A Frobenius-semilinear functor D:C→E is linearized by D∘Fr_{C₀}^{−1}. The form is data, not an automatic choice for any k-linear category.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Construction 4.17 defines the Frobenius twist C^(p) of a k-linear category by twisting its Hom spaces, and proves its universal property for Frobenius-semilinear functors. Given an F_p-form as in (4.6), it defines the semilinear self-equivalence Frob_{F_0}.

proofSteps: Base-change each Hom space and its bilinear composition. Prove the universal property, then use perfectness of k and the supplied form to identify the twist with C. Keep the inverse Frobenius on the source.
acceptance: In the one-object category with endomorphism algebra k, the tautological map sends a scalar to its Frobenius image after the form identification.
Over k=F₉ choose a∉F₃; precomposing D(a·id)=a³D(id) with inverse Frobenius makes the result a·id.
Changing the F_p-form changes the chosen self-equivalence data; without a form only C^(p) is canonical.

nodes.title: The prime-field form of normalized parity
nodes.statement: The ordinary normalized k-parity category on Gr_G has a specified F_p-form compatible with Satake and the integral split dual group. On each finite Schubert support, scalar extension on Hom and the normalized generators gives the form; the resulting semilinear Frobenius equivalence is compatible with tensor/convolution, pullback by geometric automorphisms and the normalized constant terms. A field-of-definition assertion for all arbitrary étale sheaves is unnecessary.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

proofSteps: Use the F_p-Chevalley dual group and its tilting generators, then transport the form through Satake. Check scalar extension on finite-support Hom and descent of the normalized parity generators. This must agree with the geometric form on the norm/Smith construction and its automorphism actions; the comparison is included in G2.

nodes.title: The linear base change functor
nodes.statement: For G=H^p and odd p good for Ĥ, define BC^(p):Parity^0_{(L^+G)}(Gr_G;k)→Parity^0_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;k) by descending L Psm Nm through ordinary reduction. Its Hom map is Frobenius-semilinear. Define BC=BC^(p)∘Fr_{source,F_p}^{−1}; this is k-linear and additive. Use ordinary orbit-constructible morphisms, with the proven equivariant realizations and only norm-generated intermediate C_p-morphisms. The source of descent is not the falsely asserted full C_p-equivariant reduction category.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Definition 4.18 defines BC^(p) as the unique functor filling (4.7) through modular reduction, and BC as BC^(p)∘Frob_p^{-1}. Section A.5 checks the scalar behaviour but prints the composition in the other order (finding E33).

proofSteps: Additivity and annihilation of p Hom groups let L Psm Nm factor through O-Hom tensor k. The valid non-equivariant reduction equivalence gives the functor, uniquely up to natural isomorphism. Use the selected prime-field form to cancel Frobenius on source maps. Independence of integral lifts follows from full faithfulness of the reduced ordinary Hom functor.
acceptance: BC preserves zero objects and biproducts with natural inclusions and projections.
BC(a·f)=a·BC(f), including a∈F₉\F₃; before linearization BC^(p)(a·f)=a^pBC^(p)(f).
Replacing the source by arbitrary C_p-equivariant parity objects fails the augmentation-ideal Hom test and is forbidden.

nodes.title: Hyperbolic localization and equal-characteristic constant terms
nodes.statement: Choose B_H⊃T_H and a regular dominant cocharacter κ:G_m→T_H. On Gr_H the κ-attractors are S_ν with inclusions i_ν:S_ν→Gr_H and retractions p_ν:S_ν→{t^ν}. For bounded-support κ-monodromic étale complexes define CT_H=⊕_ν Rp_{ν!}i_ν*, calculated on bounded Schubert supports, and CT_H^norm at ν by [⟨2ρ_H,ν⟩]. Here monodromic means in the triangulated subcategory generated by objects coming from κ-equivariant derived sheaves; an invariant support alone does not suffice. Define the repelling version as well and prove its natural agreement on this domain. Coefficients are k and O with the compatible adic conditions.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Section A.4 fixes a regular σ-invariant cocharacter and defines CT_G as the sum over ν of Rp_ν!i_ν^* on G_m-monodromic sheaves, with its normalized shift by ⟨2ρ,ν⟩. Display (A.1) says the shifted constant terms are t-exact and correspond to restriction to the dual torus. Remark A.1 says the modular equal-characteristic case is not completely documented.

Section 3 constructs the semi-infinite orbits and their intersections with Schubert cells (Theorem 3.2). Theorem 3.5 shows compactly supported cohomology along S_ν is concentrated in degree ⟨2ρ,ν⟩ and agrees with the costalk version along the opposite orbit. Theorem 3.6 assembles these weight functors into the cohomology functor.

Theorem 1 says that for a normal variety with a G_m-action and a weakly equivariant complex, the natural map between the attracting and repelling hyperbolic localizations is an isomorphism. Lemma 6 is the contraction lemma used in its proof. Page 2 shows by an example on C² with weights (1,−1) that some equivariance hypothesis is needed.

proofSteps: Use the imported loop/Schubert geometry but construct these equal-characteristic modular functors here. Apply Braden’s natural transformation on equivariant linear/projective ambient models containing each bounded piece; the contraction lemma and open–closed localization prove it invertible on weakly equivariant generators, then on their triangulated closure. Patch bounded supports and finite coefficient levels, using G1/G2 for O. The normalized shift convention is positive [⟨2ρ,ν⟩], so weight cohomology is in degree zero.
acceptance: For a split torus ρ=0 and the attracting loci are points; CT is the identity on its finite-supported sheaf category.
For the spherical unit supported at t^0, CT^norm has just the zero-weight copy of Λ in degree zero.
A sheaf supported on the non-invariant diagonal in A² with weights (+1,−1) need not have equal attracting and repelling localizations; monodromicity is required.
