nodes.title: Semi-infinite intersections at extreme weights
nodes.statement: For dominant λ and the chosen positive Borel, S_{w₀λ}∩Gr_H^λ is the single point t^{w₀λ}. If S_{w₀λ} meets Gr_H^μ with μ dominant in the same component, then λ≤μ in the dominance order. More generally the weights in Gr_H^μ lie in the Weyl-polytope of μ, and the intersection dimension is ⟨ρ,μ+ν⟩. These are scheme/étale-geometric statements on finite Schubert pieces, not formal consequences of a B_dR^+ Satake result.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.2, display (3.6) and the paragraph after it, p.9
sources.match: Theorem 3.2 says S_ν∩Gr^λ is nonempty exactly when ν is a weight of the irreducible representation of highest weight λ, and then has pure dimension ⟨ρ,λ+ν⟩. Display (3.6) computes S_ν∩Gr^ν in the dominant and antidominant cases, where it is a single point for antidominant ν. The following paragraph applies this to the extreme weights ν=λ and ν=w_0λ.
The proof of Lemma A.3 uses that S_{w_0λ} meets Gr^λ_H in the single point t^{w_0λ}, citing Baumann–Riche.

proofSteps: Compute the antidominant intersection using loop-unipotent factorization; the opposite positive loops fix its coweight point. Use the Schubert order and torus weight polytope for the support exclusion. Apply the equal-characteristic base-change/étale transport in G2.
acceptance: For H=GL₂ and λ=(1,0), the antidominant semi-infinite intersection with the minuscule P¹ is one point. Its dimension from ⟨ρ,λ+w₀λ⟩ is zero; a larger Schubert support cannot be excluded without dominance.

nodes.title: Normalized constant term is restriction to the dual torus
nodes.statement: CT_H^norm is exact on the k-Satake heart and sends O-flat Satake objects to O-free finite-supported weight modules. It is symmetric monoidal and corresponds under modular Satake to Res_{T̂_H}^{Ĥ}. It preserves normalized parity, where a torus parity object is a finite sum of point-supported coefficient modules in degree zero. Its construction and natural transformations commute with the relevant coefficient extensions.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Theorems 3.5–3.6 and Corollary 3.7, pp.10–12; Propositions 6.3–6.4, pp.20–21
sources.match: Theorems 3.5–3.6 give the weight functors on the spherical perverse category with arbitrary Noetherian coefficients of finite global dimension. Corollary 3.7 shows global cohomology is exact and faithful. Propositions 6.3–6.4 show that total cohomology and its weight grading are tensor functors for convolution.

Remark A.1 explains that the intertwining (A.1) of shifted constant terms with restriction to the dual torus is built into the identification of the Tannakian group. It is documented for the complex and B_dR^+ Grassmannians but not for the equal-characteristic modular one.

proofSteps: Use the semi-infinite dimension estimate and the perverse stalk/costalk inequalities to concentrate ν-cohomology in degree ⟨2ρ,ν⟩. Braden’s comparison identifies the two bounds. Fusion gives the convolution tensor decomposition of weight spaces, including the symmetry sign correction. During reconstruction of the dual group these weight functors define its torus, giving the claimed natural restriction comparison.
acceptance: For the minuscule GL₂ representation, normalized CT gives its two one-dimensional torus weights in degree zero. On the unit only weight zero remains. Tensor convolution gives the usual sum of weights.

nodes.title: Smith commutes with normalized constant term
nodes.statement: For G=H^p, take the diagonal κ-action commuting with cyclic rotation. On the bounded monodromic equivariant domains there is a natural equivalence CT_H^norm Psm≅Psm CT_G^norm in integral and mod-p Tate categories. Under the diagonal identification a fixed weight is (ν,…,ν); the G-shift p⟨2ρ_H,ν⟩ differs from the H-shift by the even integer (p−1)⟨2ρ_H,ν⟩. Use the fixed categorical periodicity isomorphism to compare them.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Using the compatibilities of Psm with pullback and pushforward from A.1.1–A.1.2, Feng states diagram (A.2): Smith intertwines CT_G and CT_H. He adds that this survives the degree shifts by the parity calculation of §4.6.3.

proofSteps: On each attracting correspondence use pullback compatibility and the compact-support Smith theorem. Restrict to fixed weights and track the componentwise normalization shifts through the chosen periodicity class. Check coherence on maps and nested supports; equality of parities by itself is not a natural isomorphism.
acceptance: At a diagonal weight ν, compute p⟨2ρ,ν⟩−⟨2ρ,ν⟩ explicitly and use the chosen two-periodicity generator. For a torus all shifts vanish. An arbitrary nonfixed weight has no fixed-locus contribution.

nodes.title: Constant terms, lifting and base change
nodes.statement: On normalized integral Tate parity objects of Gr_H, CT_H^norm commutes naturally with L after passage to the normalized torus parity category. Consequently CT_H^norm BC≅BC_T CT_G^norm naturally on ordinary normalized k-parity objects. The proof must use the graded Hom formula with composition and coefficient-change compatibility, rather than essential surjectivity of T*ε* alone.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Lemma A.2 and its proof, diagrams (A.3)–(A.5), pp.59–60
sources.match: Lemma A.2 states that four side faces of cube (A.3) commute. Its proof handles the front face through (A.4) and the right square of (A.5). It deduces the latter from the caps (4.3), essential surjectivity of inflation and the morphism formula (4.2), without carrying out the morphism-level check that this node states (finding E35).

proofSteps: For inflated ordinary parity objects compare both composites with ordinary reduced CT. Under integral-tate-hom the normalized CT map preserves the integer index, because the construction commutes with coefficients and the periodicity class. Its target is a finite sum of point-supported degree-zero modules, so positive-index ordinary Hom there is zero. Projection to index zero therefore commutes with CT on every Tate morphism. Extend across decompositions by naturality, then use the full ordinary reduction equivalence for BC, tensor compatibility for Nm and the fixed prime-field form. This avoids asserting that inflation is full. G2 includes proving the stated graded comparison in the étale realization.
acceptance: For normalized torus objects, Hom(E,F[2i]) is zero for i>0 and i<0. Check that the image of the P¹ positive-index Tate class is killed on the torus, using graded CT compatibility; objectwise essential surjectivity cannot replace this test.

nodes.title: Base change for a split torus on objects and maps
nodes.statement: For H a split torus with cocharacter lattice X_*(H), BC takes the point object at (ν₁,…,ν_p) on Gr_{H^p} to the point object at ν₁+⋯+ν_p on Gr_H. On a scalar endomorphism a it acts by a after inverse Frobenius, not a^p. On arbitrary finite sums its action is the corresponding matrix/block map. Under torus Satake this is naturally diagonal restriction.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Section A.5 reduces to H=G_m. It computes Nm of the constant sheaf at (n_1,…,n_p) as the constant sheaf at the diagonal sum, and its fixed restriction as the point sheaf at n_1+⋯+n_p. It then checks that a scalar λ becomes λ^p before inverse Frobenius restores λ.

proofSteps: The norm sums the p coweights in every factor and fixed restriction is the diagonal point. Compute the norm on scalar maps as a^p, then precompose source inverse Frobenius. Torus rational representations decompose by weights; additivity extends the scalar computation to all matrices and yields naturality.
acceptance: For H=G_m, p=3 and coweights (2,−1,4), the output is weight 5. A scalar a∈F₉ outside F₃ is unchanged after linearization; without inverse Frobenius it becomes a³.

nodes.title: Objectwise diagonal restriction
nodes.statement: For every normalized k-parity object E on Gr_{H^p}, Sat_H(BC(E)) and Res_Δ(Sat_G(E)) have naturally identified T̂_H-restrictions, once constant-term-lifting has been proved. Therefore their characters agree and the two tilting objects are isomorphic. This conclusion alone does not produce an Ĥ-equivariant natural isomorphism of functors.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Theorem 4.20 asserts that BC commutes with diagonal restriction under the parity–tilting equivalences. Section A.4 reduces this to the torus case, using Lemma A.2 and Donkin's result that tilting modules are determined by their characters; §A.5 treats the torus. The node keeps the objectwise conclusion that this argument does give.

proofSteps: Apply normalized constant terms and the torus functor comparison. Triangular tilting characters then determine the object isomorphism class. State separately which weight comparison is natural; no lifting of weight-space maps is inferred from faithfulness.
acceptance: For source external tiltings T(λ₁)⊠⋯⊠T(λ_p), the output character is the product of the factor characters. This identifies its tilting isomorphism class and its torus weights, while leaving equivariance of the chosen comparison open.

nodes.title: Equivariance of the base change comparison maps
nodes.statement: Construct, for every tilting V of Ĥ^p, an invertible Ĥ-equivariant map α_V:Sat_H BC Sat_G^{-1}(V)→Res_Δ V whose restriction to T̂_H is the natural torus/constant-term comparison and for which α_W BC(f)=Res_Δ(f) α_V for every tilting morphism f:V→W. The exact missing assertion is equivariance of the existing weight-space comparison, not equality of tilting characters.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: §A.4, the paragraph after the proof of Lemma A.2, p.60
sources.match: This paragraph deduces the top face of (A.3) from the bottom face, by faithfulness of restriction to the dual torus and character determination of tilting modules. That step does not produce Ĥ-equivariant comparison maps (finding E34); constructing them is the target here.

proofSteps: G5: prove that the weight comparison intertwines each simple-root subgroup of Ĥ, for example by constructing compatible rank-one Levi comparisons and their Chevalley generators. Then the torus and root subgroups generate Ĥ, so components are Ĥ-equivariant; their weight-level naturality proves naturality. A complete rank-one compatibility argument is not located in the read source and is not claimed here. Alternatively supply a direct tensor/fibre-functor construction with the same normalized components.
acceptance: For dual SL₂, verify the comparison commutes with the upper and lower root subgroup operators as well as the diagonal torus. A diagonal weight-space automorphism with unequal scalar entries supplies a torus-intertwiner that need not pass this test.

nodes.title: Feng’s Satake base change theorem
nodes.statement: For separably closed F of characteristic different from p, H connected reductive, G=H^p with cyclic rotation, k=Fbar_p, and odd p good for Ĥ, the k-linear additive functor BC on normalized Grassmannian parity objects corresponds, under modular Satake and the parity–tilting equivalences, to restriction along the diagonal Ĥ→Ĥ^p. The comparison is an isomorphism of functors, natural in every tilting morphism. The plan for this endpoint depends on the open equivariance target G5.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.20 and footnote 11, pp.27–28; Appendix A, pp.56–61
sources.match: Theorem 4.20 states that BC corresponds, under the parity–tilting Satake equivalences, to restriction along the diagonal Ĥ→Ĝ; footnote 11 explains why diagonal restriction preserves tilting modules. Appendix A, by Feng and Lonergan, gives the proof.

proofSteps: After G5 supplies actual equivariant comparison components, use their naturality and invertibility to identify the functors. Diagonal restriction lands in tiltings by tensor closure. The torus and objectwise results are established as separate weaker targets, so this final theorem is not silently substituted by a character identity.
acceptance: For H a torus, recover the full natural formula already proved in torus-base-change. For dual SL₂ and an external product of standard tiltings, require intertwining of both root subgroups on every component; equality of characters is insufficient.

nodes.title: Conservativity of Tate constant terms
nodes.statement: On the κ-monodromic orbit-constructible k-coefficient Tate category of Gr_H with finite Schubert support, CT_H^norm is conservative: CT(K)=0 implies K=0, hence CT detects equivalences. Extend to an ind object only when the support argument or a filtered-piece detection theorem applies; the finite-support result is enough for exactness of a fixed finite-dimensional Satake sequence.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma A.3 states that CT on the constructible orbit-stratified k-Tate category of Gr_H is conservative. The proof chooses a maximal supported stratum and evaluates at its antidominant fixed point. The proof is phrased for the ind-constructible category although the statement concerns the constructible one (finding E36).

proofSteps: Choose a maximal dominant λ among the finitely many strata supporting K. The support exclusion and extreme point calculation identify its lowest-weight constant term with the stalk at t^{w₀λ}; all other supported strata are excluded. Orbit constructibility and homogeneity show this stalk cannot vanish if K is nonzero on that stratum. Apply to a cone to detect isomorphisms.
acceptance: For a nonzero finite-support Tate object choose a maximal supported Schubert stratum and its antidominant point; CT detects that restriction. The zero object is detected as zero. Do not infer conservativity from faithfulness of a representation forgetful functor.

nodes.title: Exactness of the mod-p Smith norm on Satake
nodes.statement: For every short exact sequence 0→V′→V→V″→0 in finite-dimensional rational Rep_k(Ĥ^p), the sequence obtained by Fr^{-1}, geometric Satake, Nm and Psm is a distinguished triangle in the constructible k-Tate category, with the comparison from the cone to the third term specified by the enhanced construction. This is an exactness assertion for the composite into the Tate quotient, not exactness of Nm as an additive functor before quotienting.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma 4.21 states that the composite of inverse Frobenius, Satake, Nm and Psm sends exact sequences of representations to exact triangles in the Tate category. Section A.6 proves it with Lemma A.3, the constant-term compatibility and the splitting of torus representations, reducing to additivity.

proofSteps: Construct the cone comparison using the functorial p-cube associated to the two maps and their canonical zero composite in the perverse heart; this avoids an arbitrary cone comparison. Apply CT, which is symmetric monoidal, commutes with Smith and detects equivalences on the finite support. The representation sequence splits after restriction to a torus. Mixed cyclic terms vanish in the Tate quotient, so the torus case reduces to additive split exactness.
acceptance: For a split short exact sequence of torus representations, mixed terms form free cyclic orbits and the image triangle splits. For a nonsplit rational reductive sequence, CT makes it split; conservativity detects the enhanced cone comparison.

nodes.title: Continuous equivariantization of the parity category
nodes.statement: For a discrete group Γ acting coherently on an additive category C, define C^{BΓ} by objects with maps u_γ:γE→E satisfying the cocycle law and morphisms commuting with every u_γ. For profinite Γ and the k-parity categories here require continuity on the finite coefficient/support data; formulate O-descent as a compatible adic system. A coherently Γ-equivariant functor induces a functor of these equivariantizations. For enhanced derived sheaves use homotopy-coherent descent before taking the desired parity subcategory: fixed objects of an ordinary derived homotopy category are not asserted to equal the equivariant derived category.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Section 4.6.4 uses equivariantization in the sense of Drinfeld–Gelaki–Nikshych–Ostrik to pass from a Γ-equivariant functor to a functor between categories of Γ-equivariant objects. It stresses that equivariantizing a derived category differs from taking the equivariant derived category.

proofSteps: Write the cocycle and intertwining conditions, including coherent structure of the group action. For arithmetic descent work with continuous finite-level Galois descent and its enhancement; then restrict to the parity objects with descent data.
acceptance: For Γ trivial, C^{BΓ}≅C.
For a trivial action on finite-dimensional k-vector spaces and finite Γ, equivariant objects are actual k[Γ]-representations and intertwining maps.
For profinite Γ a discontinuous abstract action on a discrete finite-dimensional space is excluded even if its abstract cocycle equations hold.

nodes.statement: Let H descend to F₀⊂F and G=Res_{E₀/F₀}(H_{E₀}) for a cyclic degree-p extension E₀/F₀. After choosing a geometric splitting G_F≅H_F^p, Γ=Gal(F/F₀) acts compatibly with the cyclic norm construction. BC is coherently Γ-equivariant on normalized k-parity objects with the chosen prime-field form. If the natural Ĥ-comparison of feng-base-change is proved Γ-equivariant as well, its equivariantization identifies the descended BC with restriction along the diagonal map of geometric L-groups, with the same cyclotomic normalization on both sides.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma 4.22 shows BC is Aut(F/F_0)-equivariant for a cyclic Weil-restriction setup, since its constituents are. Corollary 4.23 equivariantizes Theorem 4.20 to identify the descended BC with restriction between tilting categories of geometric L-groups.

proofSteps: Reuse separable Weil-restriction splitting and the integral dual Galois action. Norm, fixed restriction, coefficient change and the chosen lifting/Frobenius comparisons commute with Γ. Descend using the full ordinary parity reduction equivalence and check the cocycle, not only a family of object isomorphisms. For the L-group comparison require the components in G5 to respect Γ; character equality is insufficient.
acceptance: For trivial Γ recover BC. For a cyclic permutation of geometric Weil-restriction factors, check the descent cocycle around the full orbit. A family of object isomorphisms without a cocycle is not descent.

nodes.title: The valid objectwise integral comparison
nodes.statement: Let F_T:Perf_S(Y;TO)→Perf_S(Y;Tk) be derived coefficient reduction, and I_k=T*ε*_k:D^b_S(Y;k)→Perf_S(Y;Tk). For a normalized integral Tate-parity object K, there is an object isomorphism I_k L(K)≅F_T(K). It is natural on morphisms arising by inflation of ordinary normalized O-parity morphisms. It is not claimed natural on every Tate morphism. Smith commutes naturally with coefficient reduction on its valid domain, without using this stronger false right face.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma 4.24 asserts that the cube (4.8), relating integral and mod-p parity, Tate and derived categories, commutes. The proof of its right face reduces to the image of the left column, which is not full there (finding E29). The node keeps the objectwise statement and naturality for inflated ordinary maps.

proofSteps: Choose the ordinary parity generator for K and use L T*ε*≅F; extend to finite sums. Ordinary inflated maps occupy index zero, where the comparison is natural. In the GL₂ minuscule closed Schubert variety P¹ with E=O[1], the class H²(P¹;k) gives an index-one Tate morphism: L kills it, whereas coefficient reduction to the k-Tate category retains it. Thus essential surjectivity cannot promote the object comparison to a natural transformation on all Tate maps.
acceptance: On the integral Tate unit the comparison is the coefficient quotient O→k. On P¹ with E=O[1], the object comparison holds while a nonzero index-one endomorphism disproves its naturality on every Tate map.

nodes.title: The integral comparison on norm-generated morphisms
nodes.statement: For D=Psm Nm on ordinary normalized O-parity objects, construct coherent object identifications F_T D(E)≅I_k L D(E) that intertwine F_T D(f) with I_k L D(f) for every ordinary parity morphism f, and are compatible with reduction and inverse Frobenius. This gives the natural back-face comparison needed by the global Tate-cohomology consumer. Only the norm-generated maps are in this target; arbitrary integral Tate maps are excluded.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.locator: Lemma 4.24, pp.29–30; proof of Proposition 5.12(i), p.39
sources.match: The proof of Proposition 5.12(i) uses the back face of cube (4.8) as a natural isomorphism of functors on tilting modules. That is the norm-image comparison targeted here (gap G4).

proofSteps: G4: control the positive-index terms of D(f) in the integral Tate Hom formula relative to coherent choices of the normalized lifts. A sufficient condition is that norm-generated morphisms have only index zero; a weaker sufficient condition is that all remaining terms are killed by F_T. Neither follows from objectwise normalization or from additivity. Supply a proof of one such condition, or a direct comparison natural in f. The P¹ counterexample prevents using the printed full-cube argument.
acceptance: Use an ordinary source morphism f, expand Psm Nm(f) in the graded Hom formula, and check the proposed square term by term. Arbitrary positive-index Tate endomorphisms are an explicit failing control; proving all norm-generated cases remains G4.

nodes.title: The Tate diagonal of a commutative algebra
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative F_p-algebra with an F_p-algebra automorphism σ satisfying σ^p=1. Let A^σ be its fixed subring, Tr(a)=Σ_iσ^i(a), and Nm(a)=∏_iσ^i(a). The image Tr(A) is an ideal of A^σ. Define T^0(A)=A^σ/Tr(A), whose underlying additive group is the pinned degree-zero Tate quotient. The rule Δ_p(a)=[Nm(a)] is a unital F_p-algebra homomorphism A→T^0(A). If A is a k-algebra and σ is k-linear, Δ_p(λa)=λ^pΔ_p(a); it is Frobenius-semilinear, not generally k-linear.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Definition 5.14 takes a commutative characteristic-p algebra with σ-action. It notes that N·A is an ideal of A^σ, defines the multiplicative norm Nm, and calls its composite with A^σ→A^σ/N·A=T^0(A) the Tate diagonal homomorphism Δ_p.

proofSteps: Prove Tr(A) is additively closed and b Tr(a)=Tr(ba) for fixed b. Expand Nm(a+b); nonconstant binary words form free cyclic orbits, and each orbit sum is a transfer. Multiplicativity and the unit are direct. Match the underlying additive quotient with H0IsoNormQuotient without claiming that existing additive Tate cohomology already supplies this ring homomorphism.
acceptance: For trivial σ, Tr=0 in characteristic p and Δ_p(a)=a^p, so over F₉ it is not the identity on all scalars.
For A=B^p with cyclic factor rotation, transfer surjects onto the diagonal invariants and T^0(A)=0, including its unit as the zero ring.
For A=k[x₀,…,x_{p−1}] with cyclic permutation, Nm(x₀)=∏x_i and every mixed orbit sum in Nm(a+b) is killed; the transfer ideal is inside A^σ, not the ideal it generates in all of A.

nodes.title: Unique extension of a Tate character
nodes.statement: Let A,σ be as above, κ a perfect field of characteristic p, and A′⊂A^σ a unital subring containing Nm(A) and Tr(A). Every unital ring homomorphism χ:A′→κ vanishing on Tr(A) extends uniquely to a unital ring homomorphism χ̃:A→κ. It is given by χ̃(a)=Frob_κ^{-1}(χ(Nm(a))). If A is a k-algebra with k-linear σ, κ=k and χ is k-linear, then χ̃ is k-linear. Taking A′=A^σ, restriction is therefore a bijection from σ-invariant k-algebra characters A→k to k-algebra characters of T^0(A); this is Treumann–Venkatesh (3.4.1).
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Lemma 5.15 says that a character of a subring A′ of A^σ containing Nm(A) and N·A, vanishing on N·A, extends uniquely to A, by χ̃(a)=χ(Nm a)^{1/p} into a perfect field. Uniqueness comes from linear independence of characters (Stacks 0CKK).

Display (3.4.1) is the case A′=A^σ and κ=k for a k-algebra: restriction gives a bijection from σ-fixed k-characters of A to characters of T^0A. It is proved by the same norm formula and linear independence. The closing remark extends the argument to values in an integral domain.

proofSteps: The additive-defect transfer formula and multiplicativity prove the displayed map is a ring homomorphism. For a′∈A′ use Nm(a′)=a′^p to check extension. Any other extension annihilates all transfers, so the sum of its p cyclic translates is zero. If its orbit had length p these would be distinct multiplicative characters, contradicting the existing linear-independence theorem; hence it is σ-invariant. Taking the p-th power then determines its value uniquely by perfectness.
acceptance: For trivial σ on A=k[x], A′=A and κ perfect, the formula Frob^{-1}(χ(a^p)) recovers χ(a). For a cyclic product algebra the transfer ideal contains 1, so no unital transfer-annihilating character to a nonzero field exists.

For A=k^p with cyclic rotation, the p coordinate characters are permuted freely, so no character is σ-invariant, matching T^0(A)=0 having no characters; for trivial σ the bijection is the identity of Hom(A,k).

nodes.title: Frobenius twist and linearization of algebras
nodes.statement: For a k-vector space W, set W^(p)=W⊗_{k,Frob}k: the same vectors with λ acting as λ^{1/p}, so that the tautological map W→W^(p) is Frobenius-semilinear. For a commutative k-algebra A, A^(p) is this twist of the underlying module with the tensor-product algebra structure. Its tautological map is Frobenius-semilinear and universal for such maps from A to commutative k-algebras. Given a specific F_p-form A₀ and A≅A₀⊗_{F_p}k, let Fr_{A₀} fix A₀ and send scalar λ to λ^p. Linearize a Frobenius-semilinear map f:A→B as f∘Fr_{A₀}^{−1}. Apply this to Δ_p to obtain a k-algebra map after choosing a form.
hypotheses: Conventions C0–C4 in the reader apply, restricted to the coefficients, support and equivariance stated here.

sources.match: Construction 5.17 defines the Frobenius twist A^(p)=A⊗_{k,Frob}k of a k-algebra and its universal property for Frobenius-semilinear homomorphisms. Given an F_p-structure, it defines the semilinear isomorphism Frob_{φ_0} and the linearization f∘Frob_{φ_0}^{-1}.

Section 2.1 defines the Frobenius twist W^(p)=W⊗_{(k,Frob)}k of a k-vector space, equivalently the same vectors with scalars acting through λ^{1/p}. Treumann and Venkatesh use it in their linkage definition (Definition 6.2, p.20).

proofSteps: Use the existing tensor-product algebra and Frobenius ring equivalence. Prove the scalar-extension universal property with the correct balancing relation; identify the twist using the given form. No canonical self-linearization is asserted in the absence of the form.
acceptance: For A=k[x] with form F_p[x], Fr fixes x and raises only coefficients to p-th powers.
For trivial σ on A=k[x], linearizing Δ_p sends x to x^p and scalars to themselves; it is not the identity endomorphism of A.
Over F₉ a scalar a outside F₃ is restored to a by source inverse Frobenius followed by the p-semilinear map.

gaps.detail: The existing normalized-adic supplier treats the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_p. Prove the extension to O=W(overline(F_p)) with enhanced limits, finite-level group-ring coefficients, common constructible stratifications and uniform Tor/cohomological intervals. In particular prove the projection-formula and derived-limit comparisons for Rf!, the ambient local Rj* bound and the conservative constructible-to-ind Tate quotient comparison. Levelwise finite-Tor assertions alone do not give these conclusions. Torsion k-coefficient Smith theory and finite-dimensional pieces do not depend on this extension.

gaps.title: Étale modular Satake and parity transport
gaps.detail: Supply the equal-characteristic scheme-theoretic modular k/O branch over arbitrary separably closed F of characteristic different from p: fusion with signs, weight-functor exactness, integral dual-group reconstruction and the needed finite-Schubert/stratum geometry. Transport the JMW/LL complex-topological parity and integral Tate Hom results, with constant local systems on strata in positive characteristic (finding E38), with their composition grading, equivariant realization, coefficient change and CT compatibility. Check the F_p-form against the geometric one. MV07 Theorem 14.1 gives a model through Z_p and scalar extension, but does not by itself document every W(k)-adic/LL compatibility. The B_dR^+ Satake roadmap is not a theorem covering this case.

gaps.title: The good-prime parity-perversity engine
gaps.detail: MR18 Corollary 1.6 uses its Theorem 1.1, an equivalence from Iwahori-constructible parity sheaves on the complex affine Grassmannian to graded exotic tilting coherent sheaves on the dual Springer resolution, with [1] corresponding to grading shift ⟨−1⟩ and E_λ to T_{−λ}. Its proof requires the modular exotic highest-weight category, Kostant–Whittaker/Soergel description and central-isogeny/product reductions. These inputs are not the characteristic-zero Springer correspondence. Establish this engine or give another proof under the same good-prime hypothesis, then the transport in G2. Do not substitute JMW16’s stronger prime bound for the promised theorem.

gaps.title: Naturality of the integral comparison on the norm image
gaps.detail: Prove the comparison F_T Psm Nm≅I_k L Psm Nm natural on all ordinary normalized integral parity maps. It suffices to prove that their Smith images have only index-zero components in the integral Tate Hom decomposition, or that every positive component is killed by coefficient reduction, with coherent choices of object identifications. Neither follows from additivity, normalization or the objectwise comparison. On the P¹ minuscule Schubert variety, a positive-index Tate morphism disproves the comparison on all Tate maps. This obligation is needed by the global Tate-cohomology consumer, not by the definition of BC.

gaps.title: A natural dual-group-equivariant comparison
gaps.detail: The CT square and character classification identify the output tilting objects, and the torus case identifies maps after torus restriction. Construct comparison components which intertwine the whole Ĥ-action and are natural in every source morphism. A sufficient route checks compatibility with each simple-root subgroup/rank-one Levi together with the torus, then uses generation of Ĥ. Faithful torus restriction only gives uniqueness of a lift, not its existence. Also check Γ-equivariance of these components for the arithmetic corollary. This is the exact gap between character equality and the natural isomorphism in Feng24 Theorem 4.20.

sourceIssues.printed: The JMW condition, required for any two finite free local systems on a stratum, is said to hold for Kac–Moody flag varieties, in particular affine flag varieties, over arbitrary separably closed fields, with a reference to JMW14 §4.1, which works over the complex numbers.
sourceIssues.correction: Over a separably closed field of positive characteristic ℓ, impose the condition, and the simple connectivity used in Lemma 4.16, only for constant local systems on the strata, equivalently for local systems equivariant under the connected positive-loop or Iwahori stabilizers. The parity sheaves of §4.5 have constant local systems on their strata, so the later arguments are unaffected.
sourceIssues.reason: A one-dimensional Bruhat cell of the affine flag variety is A¹. For d≥3 prime to ℓ and a nontrivial character ψ of F_ℓ into k^× (which exists since p≠ℓ), the Artin–Schreier sheaf L_ψ(x^d) is a rank-one local system on A¹ with H¹(A¹,L_ψ(x^d)) of dimension d−1. So Ext¹ between the constant sheaf and a finite free local system on that stratum is nonzero, and A¹ is not simply connected for k-local systems.
